context: Request: general litigation matters of the firm that had a fee-shifting provision, with the documents (for a fee-shifting playbook). Rubric: 14 qualifying matters (1006-00005, 1008-00007, 1010-00005, 1012-00006, 1019-00005, 1020-00005, 1021-00006, 1023-00002, 1024-00003, 1027-00003, 1033-00006, 1035-00004, 1038-00007, 1044-00006), one proof-document criterion each, plus a precision criterion. Several have sibling matters of the same client (1006-00004, 1008-00005, 1038-00006) that are outside the set.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Attempt 2: extraction script over 1,325 documents under litigation and agreement paths for fee-clause phrases (about 698K characters, 105 matters); a heredoc error; then a second filter for prevailing-party and fee-recovery phrases printing about 137K characters. The review flags that the phrase filter can drop differently worded clauses.

stages.note: declared: Read documents picked from the file listing. Two parallel batches of about 22 reads of settlement agreements, complaints and motions from about 20 matters picked from the filtered scan; one guessed path fails and is retried. The review flags the hand-picked subset.

stages.stage: Write the response
stages.note: Writes 16 matters (contractual or enforcement-fee clauses plus statutory examples) and lists exclusions. The review flags inconsistent counts and broadened categories.

stages.stage: Check or revise the response

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: An edit refused because no stage was open, then attempt 2 adds a row-to-category mapping.

stages.stage: Finish the run
stages.note: Calls finish.

runs.failure_point: Its phrase filters over a litigation-path subset dropped two qualifying matters, it read only part of the filtered list, excluded one qualifying matter it had read, and counted many non-qualifying matters.

divergence: All three fail, in the same pattern. Each run's path searches reached every needed matter, then a text-extraction scan plus phrase filters (T0, T1) or timed-out range scans (T2) left several needed matters out of the pool it read from; the first error sits on that scan stage in all three. Each then opened siblings of the same client in place of some needed matters, excluded needed matters whose settlements had each side bear its own fees, and counted non-qualifying matters. The reviews flagged the filter or coverage problem in every run, and the write-stage review flagged over-inclusion, but the agent kept its pool and answer.
